---
title: "Glider Reporter"
subtitle: "A guide to building reproducible reports for oceanographic gliders"
---

Glider Reporter is a client-side Quarto toolkit for turning mapped glider data
into reproducible report bundles. Your data stays in your browser while you use
the website.

## Build a report in three steps

### 1. Upload data and map fields

Open [Data Intake](./data_intake.qmd), choose a sample dataset or upload your
CSV, and map its columns to the standard glider fields. Resolve or acknowledge
validation warnings, then download `glider_field_mapping.json`.

### 2. Choose reporting functions

Use the [Function Explorer](./function_explorer.qmd) to find plots, tables, and
summaries that work with your mapped fields. Review each function's required
fields, language, sample output, and source issue.

### 3. Build and download the report

Open the [Report Builder](./report_builder.qmd), upload your field mapping,
select and order compatible functions, and choose an output format. Review the
preview, download the ZIP bundle, and place it in your local `output/`
directory before extracting and running the report.

## Contribute a reporting function

New analysis and visualization ideas are welcome.

1. Open the
   [Function submission form](https://github.com/shannonrankin/glider-reporter/issues/new?template=function_submission.yml).
2. Describe the function, its required data fields, output type, execution
   requirements, and citation.
3. Paste or link the code. R, Python, Quarto, MATLAB, Julia, other languages,
   and conceptual pseudo-code are welcome.
4. Submit the issue so maintainers and contributors can discuss, test, and add
   the function to the registry.

## Translate an existing function

Translations make reporting methods reusable across the community.

1. In the [Function Explorer](./function_explorer.qmd), open a function and
   follow its GitHub Issue link to coordinate the translation.
2. Identify the source language (such as MATLAB, pseudo-code, R, or Python) and
   the target language. R, Python, and Quarto are the supported report
   languages.
3. Preserve the method, required `snake_case` input fields, units, validation
   behavior, output type, and original citation.
4. Adapt dependencies and execution instructions for the target language.
   Confirm the result accepts a cleaned dataframe and produces an
   HTML-renderable plot, Markdown table, or summary.
5. Add the translation to the source issue for review. Entries that are not yet
   available in a supported language remain marked `needs_translation`.

## Use this repository as a template

### Fork on GitHub

1. Visit the
   [Glider Reporter repository](https://github.com/shannonrankin/glider-reporter).
2. Select **Fork**, choose an owner, and create the fork.
3. Clone your fork and enter the project:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/glider-reporter.git
   cd glider-reporter
   ```

4. Customize the data, functions, and Quarto pages, then run `quarto preview`
   to review the site locally.

### Clone without forking

```bash
git clone https://github.com/shannonrankin/glider-reporter.git
cd glider-reporter
quarto preview
```

Use a fork if you plan to keep your version on GitHub or contribute changes
upstream. Use a direct clone for local exploration.
